nodes.description: Address of the game owner; initialized to address(0) and used as the privileged role in lock, unlock, own and releaseFunds.
Boolean lock flag, initialized false; read by bet() and written by lock()/unlock().
Payable entry point that pays out 2 ether when random()%2==1, msg.value==1 ether and locked is false; performs an unchecked external call to msg.sender.
Owner-only function that sets locked = true.
Owner-only function that sets locked = false.
Ownership transfer function; sets gameOwner = owner when gameOwner is address(0) or the caller is the current owner.
Owner-only function that transfers amount * (1 ether) wei to msg.sender.
View pseudo-random generator using block.timestamp and block.difficulty via keccak256.
Payable fallback function that forwards all plain transfers to bet().
Caller-supplied address used for access control checks, as call/transfer target and as beneficiary.
Miner-controllable timestamp used as entropy source in random().
Parameter of own(address owner); becomes the new gameOwner.
Parameter of releaseFunds(uint amount); multiplied by 1 ether before transfer.
Unchecked low-level call msg.sender.call.value(2 ether)() executed before any state update; classic reentrancy sink.
msg.sender.transfer(amount * (1 ether)); multiplication can overflow and the transfer is not the only payout path.
uint256(keccak256(block.timestamp, block.difficulty)) % 256 and random()%2: weak, miner-influenceable randomness and unchecked arithmetic.

edges.reason: lock() reads gameOwner to authorize the caller before setting locked.
unlock() reads gameOwner to authorize the caller before clearing locked.
own() reads gameOwner to decide whether the caller may claim ownership.
releaseFunds() reads gameOwner to authorize the payout to msg.sender.
msg.sender is compared against gameOwner in lock(), so caller identity controls the write to locked.
msg.sender is compared against gameOwner in unlock(), so caller identity controls the write to locked.
msg.sender is compared against gameOwner in own(), letting a non-owner claim ownership while gameOwner == address(0).
msg.sender is used both as the authorization subject and as the transfer recipient in releaseFunds().
msg.sender is the target of the external call, so the untrusted caller chooses the code executed before the bet settles.
msg.sender is the destination of the value transfer in releaseFunds().
No self-reference needed; placeholder removed for clarity.
The owner parameter of own() is written into the gameOwner state variable.
own() writes gameOwner without guarding against re-claim when the owner address is zero.
lock() writes locked = true, and the guard depends on an equality check with a mutable owner address.
unlock() writes locked = false under the same owner equality guard.
bet() reads the locked flag as part of its payout condition.
bet() consumes the return value of random() to decide whether to pay out.
random() performs the keccak256 modulo arithmetic that produces the payout decision value.
block.timestamp feeds the randomness computation, making the outcome miner-influenceable (timestamp dependency).
bet() executes the external call while the contract still holds the 2 ether payout and no state has been updated.
The external call to msg.sender can re-enter the contract through the payable fallback function.
The fallback function forwards control to bet(), allowing the attacker to re-run the payout path before the first bet finishes.
The amount parameter is multiplied by 1 ether inside the transfer expression, where overflow is unchecked under solc 0.4.x.
releaseFunds() executes the unchecked multiplication and transfer of amount * (1 ether).

normalization_plan.reason: The owner parameter exists only inside own(); it is a transient value that flows directly into the gameOwner state variable written by that function.
The amount parameter exists only inside releaseFunds(); it is a transient value consumed by the transfer operation of that function.
